div.div:
Estimates (assumptions)
• One event for all clients, up to 10 events/s, no loss allowed
• 15,000 / 3 = ~5,000 connections per instance
• Fan-out: 10 × 15,000 = 150,000 sends/s
• Memory: 20–50 KB per connection → up to ~750 MB per cluster
Options and their cost
• Redis Pub/Sub: simple. Cost — at-most-once, no history for catch-up
• Redis Streams (chosen): the stream is a catch-up buffer by lastEventId. Cost — MAXLEN tuning, more complex
• Managed (API Gateway, Centrifugo, Ably): cost — money, vendor lock-in
Deploy
SIGTERM → readiness 503 → httpServer.close() → close 500 connections every 5 s (code 1001). Client — backoff + jitter. terminationGracePeriodSeconds and deregistration_delay longer than the drain window.
After reconnect
• Subscribe to live first, then catch up from the stream, dedup by id
• Gap longer than the buffer — snapshot via GET /state
• Subscriptions (rooms) lived in the old instance's memory — restore them
Failures
• Redis down — no cross-instance delivery or catch-up. Sentinel / Multi-AZ, then snapshot
• Slow client — cap bufferedAmount, otherwise instance memory grows
• Instance died without close — the client notices via heartbeat (~45 s)
What breaks first at ×10 (150,000)
1. CPU on fan-out: 1.5M sends/s — batching, send only changes
2. Memory ~7.5 GB, ulimit -n, load balancer limits
3. Thundering herd on deploy
